standard_prerequisites.name: A derived limit of objects on which the elements of an ideal act nilpotently is derived complete, so the object K = R-lim K_n is derived complete
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the first conclusion of the lemma, namely that K is a derived complete object of the bounded below derived category.

standard_prerequisites.name: A complex of modules over the quotient by a power of an ideal representing a given object can be chosen free with a prescribed vanishing bound, and matching maps between the reductions can be lifted to maps of complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the system of complexes P_n of free modules with reductions isomorphic to the previous term.

standard_prerequisites.name: The derived limit of the system is represented by the limit of the complexes, and the limit of a system of flat modules with surjective transition maps is flat
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies K with the limit complex P and shows that P is a bounded above complex of flat modules, so that K tensor A over I^t is represented by P tensor A over I^t and the termwise limit can be computed.

core_obligations: Observe that K = R-lim K_n is derived complete with respect to I, using the criterion that a derived limit of objects on which the elements of the ideal act nilpotently is derived complete (proof lines 28485-28487).

Assume H^i(K_1) = 0 for i greater than b, choose a complex P_1 of free modules over A over I representing K_1 with P_1^i = 0 for i greater than b, and lift the transition maps inductively to maps P_n -> P_{n-1} inducing isomorphisms of complexes P_n over I^{n-1} P_n onto P_{n-1} (proof lines 28490-28497).

Represent K by the limit complex P = lim P_n, note that the P_n are uniformly bounded above complexes of flat modules with termwise surjective transition maps, and conclude that P is a bounded above complex of flat A-modules (proof lines 28500-28507).

Use flatness of P to represent K tensor A over I^t by P tensor A over I^t, write that as the termwise limit of the P_n tensor A over I^t, and observe that the transition maps become isomorphisms for n at least t, so the limit is P_t, which represents K_t and gives the required isomorphism (proof lines 28508-28516).
proof_roadmap: Get derived completeness of K from the general criterion on derived limits (proof lines 28485-28487).
Build complexes P_n of free modules over the successive quotients with reductions isomorphic to P_{n-1}, starting from a bounded above representative of K_1 (proof lines 28490-28497).
Represent K by the limit of the P_n and check that this limit is a bounded above complex of flat modules (proof lines 28500-28507).
Compute K tensor A over I^t as the limit of the reductions, which stabilizes at P_t, and conclude the second assertion (proof lines 28508-28516).
difficulty_reason: The statement takes a ring A, an ideal I, objects K_n of the derived categories of the quotients A over I^n with compatible transition maps, and three hypotheses (Noetherianity, boundedness above, and the reduction isomorphisms), and concludes both that the derived limit K is derived complete and that reducing K modulo I^n recovers K_n (statement lines 28470-28483). The proof combines a general criterion with an explicit construction: derived completeness comes from the criterion on derived limits, while the second assertion requires choosing bounded above complexes of free modules over each quotient and lifting the transition maps so that the reductions are honest isomorphisms of complexes, after which K is the limit of the system and that limit is a bounded above complex of flat modules, so that the reductions can be computed termwise and the system stabilizes at the n-th term (proof lines 28485-28516). The stabilization step is what makes the reduction of K isomorphic to K_n, and it depends on the strictness of the lifted maps.
